response.query: What priors, ROPE bounds, and hierarchical model formula (likelihoods and link functions) best balance power and conservatism for our Bayesian analysis of composite R?
response.answer: Use weakly informative priors, ROPE bounds around zero for conservativeness, and a hierarchical model with normal likelihoods and identity link for balanced power and conservatism.

results.content: # Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Innovation Outcomes: An Applied AI Approach Building upon this framework, we further hypothesize (H2) that tree-based ensemble learning methods (Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM) will outperform individual models (Linear Regression, SVM, and ANN). Machine learning models applied to predict innovation outcomes based on company innovation activities will exhibit differential performance across key predictive metrics, largely driven by each model’s inherent algorithmic properties and alignment with the dataset. Ensemble learning methods (Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM) will yield superior predictive performance compared to individual models (Linear Regression, SVM, and ANN) in forecasting innovation outcomes from firm-level innovation activities. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) will not significantly surpass simpler models (e.g., Linear Regression and SVM) in predicting innovation outcomes, primarily due to the limited size and binary nature of the dataset.
